analysis:
Both changed files are test-only. Qwen35CheckpointRetentionLiveTests.swift (head lines 113-136) changes the expectation of the live test targetOneChunkBelowDeepestIsKept. It now expects the retained positions [2048, 4096, latest], where latest is derived from the prompt length minus a 64-token end-of-prompt margin. That replaces the old expectation of 6144 as the deepest position. The test also requires latest - 6144 >= 1024 (the SSD benefit floor). QwenVLMTargetExtractionTests.swift (head lines 335-366) adds a unit test, endOfPromptBoundaryRequiresDensePagedSSD. It asserts that EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens returns a value only for the dense Qwen35Model on a paged backend with a paged SSD store. It must return nil for MoE, contiguous backend, nil store and a contiguous store, and demandedCaptureBoundaryMinimumTokens must stay nil for dense.

No production code is in the supplied units, so no runtime security behavior changes here. The tests point to a production change elsewhere in the PR: an end-of-prompt (demandedLatest) checkpoint donation to the SSD prefix cache, which the tests treat as gated on the SSD store and its floor. That change is not visible in this batch. Relevant threat model: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, per-donation gate, 30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed names, cacheSalt scoping). The integration pass should check, in the unseen production files (EngineV2Factory, CBv2 scheduler, SSDPrefixCache), the following:
- The new boundary still respects the per-donation gate (adoption bound plus 1024 benefit floor).
- The new boundary still carries the cacheSalt in the lookup tag.
- Nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed tag is persisted.
- The MoE exclusion is enforced in production.
- The extra donation does not widen at-rest exposure or write wear beyond the T-041 sign-off.

The tests do assert the gating on store, backend and model type. I report no findings, since no security regression is evidenced in the test code.
